replacement_request.generation_project_description:
The system supports the management of an Ethical Purchasing Group (EPS), known in Italian as a Gruppo di Acquisto Solidale (GAS), associated with a km-zero fruit and vegetable store. The purpose of the system is to connect groups of customers with local farmers and store employees, supporting a conscious purchasing process based on knowledge of product origin, quality, characteristics, availability, and price.

The operating cycle of the purchasing group is organized on a weekly basis. Farmers provide estimates of the products they can supply between Friday at noon and Saturday morning. For each available product, farmers specify the product type, quantity, price, and optionally additional crop characteristics such as size, quality, or ripeness.

The information system maintains a catalogue of products containing descriptions, photographs, the unit of measurement used for sale, and the minimum and maximum quantities that can be ordered. Each availability entered by a farmer refers to one of the products contained in the catalogue.

Customers can browse the offers provided by the different farmers and place orders by selecting products and specifying the desired quantities. Customers are representatives of purchasing groups, such as families or groups of people, and only the registered representative of each group can submit an order.

Orders can be entered directly by customers through the web system or by store employees on behalf of customers. Before an order can be confirmed, the system checks that the quantities selected respect the minimum order constraints defined for each product. If the minimum quantities are not met, the customer must modify the order. After completion, the system sends an order summary to the customer by email.

Customer orders initially remain in an entered state until farmers confirm the actual quantities available by Monday morning. If the available quantities are sufficient to satisfy all orders, the orders are confirmed. When the available quantity of a product is insufficient, the system applies precedence rules based on customer priority and removes unavailable quantities from lower-priority orders.

Orders modified because of limited product availability are placed in a modified state and must be reviewed and explicitly accepted by customers. If every product in an order becomes unavailable, the order is cancelled.

After farmers confirm product availability, the system automatically performs payment for the quantities actually included in the order. Payments are made through a personal virtual wallet associated with each customer. Customers can recharge their wallet through the store at any time.

If a customer's wallet balance is insufficient immediately after order placement, the customer receives an email warning, but the order remains valid. If the balance is insufficient when the automatic payment is executed, the customer receives an SMS and has until Monday evening to recharge the wallet. If the required balance is still unavailable at that time, the order is cancelled.

Once payment has been successfully completed, customers can reserve a time slot for collecting their products from the store. Store employees can view the pickup schedule at the beginning of their shifts and prepare the packages corresponding to customer orders. When a customer arrives, the employee confirms the collection of the order.

If a customer fails to collect the order at the scheduled time, the system sends an SMS reminder. If the order has not been collected by Friday, the order is marked as forfeited and the customer's fair-play score is updated.

Farmers deliver their products to the store by Tuesday evening. Store employees confirm the receipt of the delivered quantities. If the goods have not arrived by 4 p.m. on Tuesday, the system sends an SMS reminder. If the goods have still not been delivered by 8 p.m., the related customer orders are updated, the missing amount is credited back to the affected customers with an additional 20 percent bonus, and the customers are informed of the delivery problem.

The system maintains a fair-play score for each customer. The score represents the reliability of the customer with respect to previous orders and is used as a precedence criterion when product availability is insufficient. The score is computed from the number of completed orders, reminders received, forfeited pickups, and modified orders. Customers with higher fair-play scores are given precedence over customers with lower scores when limited quantities must be allocated among competing orders.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
The system supports the management of an Ethical Purchasing Group (EPS), known in Italian as a Gruppo di Acquisto Solidale (GAS), associated with a km-zero fruit and vegetable store. The purpose of the system is to connect groups of customers with local farmers and store employees, supporting a conscious purchasing process based on knowledge of product origin, quality, characteristics, availability, and price.

The operating cycle of the purchasing group is organized on a weekly basis. Farmers provide estimates of the products they can supply between Friday at noon and Saturday morning. For each available product, farmers specify the product type, quantity, price, and optionally additional crop characteristics such as size, quality, or ripeness.

The information system maintains a catalogue of products containing descriptions, photographs, the unit of measurement used for sale, and the minimum and maximum quantities that can be ordered. Each availability entered by a farmer refers to one of the products contained in the catalogue.

Customers can browse the offers provided by the different farmers and place orders by selecting products and specifying the desired quantities. Customers are representatives of purchasing groups, such as families or groups of people, and only the registered representative of each group can submit an order.

Orders can be entered directly by customers through the web system or by store employees on behalf of customers. Before an order can be confirmed, the system checks that the quantities selected respect the minimum order constraints defined for each product. If the minimum quantities are not met, the customer must modify the order. After completion, the system sends an order summary to the customer by email.

Customer orders initially remain in an entered state until farmers confirm the actual quantities available by Monday morning. If the available quantities are sufficient to satisfy all orders, the orders are confirmed. When the available quantity of a product is insufficient, the system applies precedence rules based on customer priority and removes unavailable quantities from lower-priority orders.

Orders modified because of limited product availability are placed in a modified state and must be reviewed and explicitly accepted by customers. If every product in an order becomes unavailable, the order is cancelled.

After farmers confirm product availability, the system automatically performs payment for the quantities actually included in the order. Payments are made through a personal virtual wallet associated with each customer. Customers can recharge their wallet through the store at any time.

If a customer's wallet balance is insufficient immediately after order placement, the customer receives an email warning, but the order remains valid. If the balance is insufficient when the automatic payment is executed, the customer receives an SMS and has until Monday evening to recharge the wallet. If the required balance is still unavailable at that time, the order is cancelled.

Once payment has been successfully completed, customers can reserve a time slot for collecting their products from the store. Store employees can view the pickup schedule at the beginning of their shifts and prepare the packages corresponding to customer orders. When a customer arrives, the employee confirms the collection of the order.

If a customer fails to collect the order at the scheduled time, the system sends an SMS reminder. If the order has not been collected by Friday, the order is marked as forfeited and the customer's fair-play score is updated.

Farmers deliver their products to the store by Tuesday evening. Store employees confirm the receipt of the delivered quantities. If the goods have not arrived by 4 p.m. on Tuesday, the system sends an SMS reminder. If the goods have still not been delivered by 8 p.m., the related customer orders are updated, the missing amount is credited back to the affected customers with an additional 20 percent bonus, and the customers are informed of the delivery problem.

The system maintains a fair-play score for each customer. The score represents the reliability of the customer with respect to previous orders and is used as a precedence criterion when product availability is insufficient. The score is computed from the number of completed orders, reminders received, forfeited pickups, and modified orders. Customers with higher fair-play scores are given precedence over customers with lower scores when limited quantities must be allocated among competing orders.

hlg_1c190ea7f86685cf_001.rationale: llg_001 enables customers to check wallet balance and payment status, which supports awareness of fund availability. llg_002 enables real-time payment notifications, enhancing transparency. llg_003 introduces a grace period mechanism for insufficient funds, adding a customer-centric recovery path. llg_004 and llg_005 define two distinct recharge channels (in-store and online), preserving the modality of payment method and location. llg_006 introduces partial payment capability, which is materially different from full payments and must be explicitly included to avoid misrepresentation of scope.
hlg_1c190ea7f86685cf_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to monitor wallet balances, receive payment notifications, manage insufficient funds with grace periods, recharge wallets via in-store terminals or online transfers, and process partial payments for orders.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Check wallet balance and payment status
Handle insufficient balance with grace period

hlg_2cf58a471a47b2bf_001.rationale: llg_001 adds the capability to record transaction details and enforce payment rules via API. llg_002 adds the capability to enforce a pickup forfeit policy, deducting from wallet or marking as forfeited via API. Together, they define a system that enforces financial obligations tied to transactional events — specifically payments and pickup-related forfeits — through API-mediated enforcement, with no inferred or generalized functionality beyond these two distinct but related capabilities.
hlg_2cf58a471a47b2bf_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Record and enforce transactional obligations including payment and pickup forfeit policies via API-driven enforcement mechanisms.

hlg_45d7b64c9eb54357_001.rationale: llg_001 enables the customer to select a pickup time slot based on store availability; llg_002 ensures the customer receives a reminder notification before the pickup time to confirm attendance; llg_003 ensures the customer is notified if they miss their pickup time and is informed of the forfeit policy consequences — which introduces an unrelated or broader capability (enforcement of policy consequences) that must be explicitly included to expose the mismatch.
hlg_45d7b64c9eb54357_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to schedule, be reminded of, and be notified about missed pickup events for product pickup at stores, including enforcement of forfeit policies upon missed pickups.

hlg_5c82e14395e9d14b_001.rationale: llg_001 enables automatic prioritization of customer orders during shortages based on fair-play score; llg_002 enables customers to view their fair-play score for transparency; llg_003 enables the system to calculate and update the fair-play score via API using order history, reminders, or penalties. Together, these form a closed-loop system of score computation, display, and prioritization — with no inferred functionality or hidden parent goal.
hlg_5c82e14395e9d14b_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a dynamic customer prioritization system during shortages that calculates, updates, and displays a fair-play score to determine order priority and enable customer self-service visibility.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Prioritize customer based on fair-play score

hlg_5f093c1983a0bd77_001.rationale: llg_001 contributes the capability to allow customers to access and view product origin details, including quality certifications and availability status, which collectively define the complete scope of this high-level goal.
hlg_5f093c1983a0bd77_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to view product origin details, quality certifications, and availability status on product pages.

hlg_8cc6881ea295c041_001.rationale: llg_001 enables the purchasing group representative to submit orders using unique credentials or group ID, establishing the authorization mechanism. llg_002 ensures that before submission, the system verifies the representative’s identity via two-factor authentication or group approval workflow, adding a mandatory verification step. Together, they define a secure, identity-verified order submission process for authorized representatives.
hlg_8cc6881ea295c041_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable authorized purchasing group representatives to submit orders while ensuring their identity is verified before submission.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Authorize group representative to submit orders

hlg_91b57471207e9b44_001.rationale: llg_001 enables customers to submit orders with minimum quantity constraints; llg_002 allows modification of existing orders by altering quantities or items; llg_003 triggers confirmation and system validation; llg_004 introduces a distinct capability to notify customers of availability-driven changes and provide API-based acceptance/rejection, which is materially different from the other goals and must be explicitly included.
hlg_91b57471207e9b44_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to submit, modify, confirm, and receive notifications for order changes due to insufficient availability, while ensuring all orders meet minimum quantity requirements.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Submit an order with minimum quantity
Notify customer of order changes due to insufficient availability

hlg_c12fcb1e0bd72453_001.rationale: llg_001 adds notification to farmers with automatic 20% bonus credit on delays; llg_002 adds notification to customers with estimated resolution time; llg_003 adds automatic 20% bonus credit for missing amounts; llg_004 adds order cancellation and 20% bonus credit for late deliveries — all via API. These capabilities are distinct and must be preserved as they represent different actors (farmer vs. customer), different actions (notify, cancel, credit), and different outcomes (bonus, resolution time).
hlg_c12fcb1e0bd72453_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Automatically notify farmers and customers of delivery delays, cancel late orders, credit back missing amounts with a 20% bonus, and provide estimated resolution times via API.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Automatically credit back missing amount with bonus
Cancel orders and credit wallets with 20% bonus if deliveries are late

hlg_d714bbf6da86e761_001.rationale: llg_001 enables store employees to view and manage pending orders for fulfillment; llg_002 adds the capability to coordinate pickup logistics including time and location; llg_003 introduces payment processing and wallet balance updates via system API; llg_004 adds the capability to confirm delivery status and update system records. Together, these cover the full lifecycle of order fulfillment from initiation to delivery confirmation, with explicit handling of pickup logistics and payment integration.
hlg_d714bbf6da86e761_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable store employees to manage end-to-end order fulfillment, including coordination of product pickup, processing customer payments, and confirming delivery status to update system records.

hlg_d7aace6841b88a6b_001.rationale: llg_001 enables initial submission of product availability estimates for dynamic allocation; llg_002 adds real-time update capability via API to reflect stock or delivery changes; llg_003 introduces a mandatory Monday-morning confirmation of final quantities available for order, which is a distinct lifecycle phase and deadline not covered by the other goals.
hlg_d7aace6841b88a6b_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable farmers to submit, update, and confirm product availability estimates for dynamic allocation and order fulfillment, with real-time updates and a Monday-morning confirmation deadline.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Confirm final product quantities available for order

decisions.rationale: The goal 'Support efficient order management and allocation' is documented in the project description, focusing on facilitating the submission, modification, confirmation of customer orders while respecting minimum quantity constraints.

The goal 'Enable seamless payment and wallet management' is documented in the project description, allowing customers to securely manage virtual wallets, receive timely payment notifications, and handle insufficient balances with grace periods.

The goal 'Optimize product pickup scheduling and collection' is documented in the project description, providing customers with time slots for product collection, notifying them of missed pickups, and enforcing forfeit policies to maintain system reliability.

The goal 'Maintain accurate inventory and availability tracking' is documented in the project description, allowing farmers to submit product availability estimates and enabling the system to dynamically adjust order fulfillment based on real-time availability.
The goal 'Support fair and transparent allocation during shortages' is documented in the project description, using a fair-play score system to prioritize customers during product shortages.

The goal 'Enable efficient store operations and order fulfillment' is documented in the project description, allowing store employees to manage orders, coordinate pickups, handle payments, and manage delivery confirmations.

The goal 'Provide timely delivery and customer notification' is documented in the project description, alerting farmers and customers of delivery delays, automatically crediting back missing amounts with bonus, and maintaining transparency about delivery status.

The goal 'Ensure reliable and fair transactional fulfillment' is documented in the project description, maintaining customer trust by enforcing payment and pickup obligations, applying fair-play scoring to prioritize reliable customers during product shortages.
The goal 'Support group-based purchasing and representative authorization' is documented in the project description, enabling only registered representatives of purchasing groups to submit orders.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
The system supports the management of an Ethical Purchasing Group (EPS), known in Italian as a Gruppo di Acquisto Solidale (GAS), associated with a km-zero fruit and vegetable store. The purpose of the system is to connect groups of customers with local farmers and store employees, supporting a conscious purchasing process based on knowledge of product origin, quality, characteristics, availability, and price.

The operating cycle of the purchasing group is organized on a weekly basis. Farmers provide estimates of the products they can supply between Friday at noon and Saturday morning. For each available product, farmers specify the product type, quantity, price, and optionally additional crop characteristics such as size, quality, or ripeness.

The information system maintains a catalogue of products containing descriptions, photographs, the unit of measurement used for sale, and the minimum and maximum quantities that can be ordered. Each availability entered by a farmer refers to one of the products contained in the catalogue.

Customers can browse the offers provided by the different farmers and place orders by selecting products and specifying the desired quantities. Customers are representatives of purchasing groups, such as families or groups of people, and only the registered representative of each group can submit an order.

Orders can be entered directly by customers through the web system or by store employees on behalf of customers. Before an order can be confirmed, the system checks that the quantities selected respect the minimum order constraints defined for each product. If the minimum quantities are not met, the customer must modify the order. After completion, the system sends an order summary to the customer by email.

Customer orders initially remain in an entered state until farmers confirm the actual quantities available by Monday morning. If the available quantities are sufficient to satisfy all orders, the orders are confirmed. When the available quantity of a product is insufficient, the system applies precedence rules based on customer priority and removes unavailable quantities from lower-priority orders.

Orders modified because of limited product availability are placed in a modified state and must be reviewed and explicitly accepted by customers. If every product in an order becomes unavailable, the order is cancelled.

After farmers confirm product availability, the system automatically performs payment for the quantities actually included in the order. Payments are made through a personal virtual wallet associated with each customer. Customers can recharge their wallet through the store at any time.

If a customer's wallet balance is insufficient immediately after order placement, the customer receives an email warning, but the order remains valid. If the balance is insufficient when the automatic payment is executed, the customer receives an SMS and has until Monday evening to recharge the wallet. If the required balance is still unavailable at that time, the order is cancelled.

Once payment has been successfully completed, customers can reserve a time slot for collecting their products from the store. Store employees can view the pickup schedule at the beginning of their shifts and prepare the packages corresponding to customer orders. When a customer arrives, the employee confirms the collection of the order.

If a customer fails to collect the order at the scheduled time, the system sends an SMS reminder. If the order has not been collected by Friday, the order is marked as forfeited and the customer's fair-play score is updated.

Farmers deliver their products to the store by Tuesday evening. Store employees confirm the receipt of the delivered quantities. If the goods have not arrived by 4 p.m. on Tuesday, the system sends an SMS reminder. If the goods have still not been delivered by 8 p.m., the related customer orders are updated, the missing amount is credited back to the affected customers with an additional 20 percent bonus, and the customers are informed of the delivery problem.

The system maintains a fair-play score for each customer. The score represents the reliability of the customer with respect to previous orders and is used as a precedence criterion when product availability is insufficient. The score is computed from the number of completed orders, reminders received, forfeited pickups, and modified orders. Customers with higher fair-play scores are given precedence over customers with lower scores when limited quantities must be allocated among competing orders.

hlg_1c190ea7f86685cf_001.rationale: llg_001 enables customers to check wallet balance and payment status, which supports awareness of fund availability. llg_002 enables real-time payment notifications, enhancing transparency. llg_003 introduces a grace period mechanism for insufficient funds, adding a customer-centric recovery path. llg_004 and llg_005 define two distinct recharge channels (in-store and online), preserving the modality of payment method and location. llg_006 introduces partial payment capability, which is materially different from full payments and must be explicitly included to avoid misrepresentation of scope.
hlg_1c190ea7f86685cf_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to monitor wallet balances, receive payment notifications, manage insufficient funds with grace periods, recharge wallets via in-store terminals or online transfers, and process partial payments for orders.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Check wallet balance and payment status
Handle insufficient balance with grace period

hlg_45d7b64c9eb54357_001.rationale: llg_001 enables the customer to select a pickup time slot based on store availability; llg_002 ensures the customer receives a reminder notification before the pickup time to confirm attendance; llg_003 ensures the customer is notified if they miss their pickup time and is informed of the forfeit policy consequences — which introduces an unrelated or broader capability (enforcement of policy consequences) that must be explicitly included to expose the mismatch.
hlg_45d7b64c9eb54357_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to schedule, be reminded of, and be notified about missed pickup events for product pickup at stores, including enforcement of forfeit policies upon missed pickups.

hlg_54413bcf2604b197_001.rationale: llg_001 adds transaction recording and payment enforcement; llg_002 adds enforcement of pickup forfeit policies including wallet deductions or marking as forfeited; llg_003 adds automatic fair-play score updates triggered by missed pickups; llg_004 adds fair-play score-based prioritization during shortages; llg_005 adds penalty or bonus management for forfeited orders based on delivery status and behavior. All five capabilities are distinct and must be preserved as they represent different lifecycle phases and outcomes.
hlg_54413bcf2604b197_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Record transactions and enforce payment, enforce pickup forfeit policies, update fair-play scores based on pickup forfeiture, apply fair-play scoring for order prioritization during shortages, and manage forfeited order penalties or bonuses via API.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Update fair-play score based on pickup forfeiture
Apply fair-play scoring for order prioritization during shortages
Manage forfeited order penalties or bonuses

hlg_5c82e14395e9d14b_001.rationale: llg_001 enables automatic prioritization of customer orders during shortages based on fair-play score; llg_002 enables customers to view their fair-play score for transparency; llg_003 enables the system to calculate and update the fair-play score via API using order history, reminders, or penalties. Together, these form a closed-loop system of score computation, display, and prioritization — with no inferred functionality or hidden parent goal.
hlg_5c82e14395e9d14b_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a dynamic customer prioritization system during shortages that calculates, updates, and displays a fair-play score to determine order priority and enable customer self-service visibility.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Prioritize customer based on fair-play score

hlg_5f093c1983a0bd77_001.rationale: llg_001 contributes the capability to allow customers to access and view product origin details, including quality certifications and availability status, which collectively define the complete scope of this high-level goal.
hlg_5f093c1983a0bd77_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to view product origin details, quality certifications, and availability status on product pages.

hlg_8cc6881ea295c041_001.rationale: llg_001 enables the purchasing group representative to submit orders using unique credentials or group ID, establishing the authorization mechanism. llg_002 ensures that before submission, the system verifies the representative’s identity via two-factor authentication or group approval workflow, adding a mandatory verification step. Together, they define a secure, identity-verified order submission process for authorized representatives.
hlg_8cc6881ea295c041_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable authorized purchasing group representatives to submit orders while ensuring their identity is verified before submission.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Authorize group representative to submit orders

hlg_91b57471207e9b44_001.rationale: llg_001 enables customers to submit orders with minimum quantity constraints; llg_002 allows modification of existing orders by altering quantities or items; llg_003 triggers confirmation and system validation; llg_004 introduces a distinct capability to notify customers of availability-driven changes and provide API-based acceptance/rejection, which is materially different from the other goals and must be explicitly included.
hlg_91b57471207e9b44_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to submit, modify, confirm, and receive notifications for order changes due to insufficient availability, while ensuring all orders meet minimum quantity requirements.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Submit an order with minimum quantity
Notify customer of order changes due to insufficient availability

hlg_c12fcb1e0bd72453_001.rationale: llg_001 adds notification to farmers with automatic 20% bonus credit on delays; llg_002 adds notification to customers with estimated resolution time; llg_003 adds automatic 20% bonus credit for missing amounts; llg_004 adds order cancellation and 20% bonus credit for late deliveries — all via API. These capabilities are distinct and must be preserved as they represent different actors (farmer vs. customer), different actions (notify, cancel, credit), and different outcomes (bonus, resolution time).
hlg_c12fcb1e0bd72453_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Automatically notify farmers and customers of delivery delays, cancel late orders, credit back missing amounts with a 20% bonus, and provide estimated resolution times via API.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Automatically credit back missing amount with bonus
Cancel orders and credit wallets with 20% bonus if deliveries are late

hlg_d714bbf6da86e761_001.rationale: llg_001 enables store employees to view and manage pending orders for fulfillment; llg_002 adds the capability to coordinate pickup logistics including time and location; llg_003 introduces payment processing and wallet balance updates via system API; llg_004 adds the capability to confirm delivery status and update system records. Together, these cover the full lifecycle of order fulfillment from initiation to delivery confirmation, with explicit handling of pickup logistics and payment integration.
hlg_d714bbf6da86e761_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable store employees to manage end-to-end order fulfillment, including coordination of product pickup, processing customer payments, and confirming delivery status to update system records.

hlg_d7aace6841b88a6b_001.rationale: llg_001 enables initial submission of product availability estimates for dynamic allocation; llg_002 adds real-time update capability via API to reflect stock or delivery changes; llg_003 introduces a mandatory Monday-morning confirmation of final quantities available for order, which is a distinct lifecycle phase and deadline not covered by the other goals.
hlg_d7aace6841b88a6b_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable farmers to submit, update, and confirm product availability estimates for dynamic allocation and order fulfillment, with real-time updates and a Monday-morning confirmation deadline.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Confirm final product quantities available for order

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
The system supports the management of an Ethical Purchasing Group (EPS), known in Italian as a Gruppo di Acquisto Solidale (GAS), associated with a km-zero fruit and vegetable store. The purpose of the system is to connect groups of customers with local farmers and store employees, supporting a conscious purchasing process based on knowledge of product origin, quality, characteristics, availability, and price.

The operating cycle of the purchasing group is organized on a weekly basis. Farmers provide estimates of the products they can supply between Friday at noon and Saturday morning. For each available product, farmers specify the product type, quantity, price, and optionally additional crop characteristics such as size, quality, or ripeness.

The information system maintains a catalogue of products containing descriptions, photographs, the unit of measurement used for sale, and the minimum and maximum quantities that can be ordered. Each availability entered by a farmer refers to one of the products contained in the catalogue.

Customers can browse the offers provided by the different farmers and place orders by selecting products and specifying the desired quantities. Customers are representatives of purchasing groups, such as families or groups of people, and only the registered representative of each group can submit an order.

Orders can be entered directly by customers through the web system or by store employees on behalf of customers. Before an order can be confirmed, the system checks that the quantities selected respect the minimum order constraints defined for each product. If the minimum quantities are not met, the customer must modify the order. After completion, the system sends an order summary to the customer by email.

Customer orders initially remain in an entered state until farmers confirm the actual quantities available by Monday morning. If the available quantities are sufficient to satisfy all orders, the orders are confirmed. When the available quantity of a product is insufficient, the system applies precedence rules based on customer priority and removes unavailable quantities from lower-priority orders.

Orders modified because of limited product availability are placed in a modified state and must be reviewed and explicitly accepted by customers. If every product in an order becomes unavailable, the order is cancelled.

After farmers confirm product availability, the system automatically performs payment for the quantities actually included in the order. Payments are made through a personal virtual wallet associated with each customer. Customers can recharge their wallet through the store at any time.

If a customer's wallet balance is insufficient immediately after order placement, the customer receives an email warning, but the order remains valid. If the balance is insufficient when the automatic payment is executed, the customer receives an SMS and has until Monday evening to recharge the wallet. If the required balance is still unavailable at that time, the order is cancelled.

Once payment has been successfully completed, customers can reserve a time slot for collecting their products from the store. Store employees can view the pickup schedule at the beginning of their shifts and prepare the packages corresponding to customer orders. When a customer arrives, the employee confirms the collection of the order.

If a customer fails to collect the order at the scheduled time, the system sends an SMS reminder. If the order has not been collected by Friday, the order is marked as forfeited and the customer's fair-play score is updated.

Farmers deliver their products to the store by Tuesday evening. Store employees confirm the receipt of the delivered quantities. If the goods have not arrived by 4 p.m. on Tuesday, the system sends an SMS reminder. If the goods have still not been delivered by 8 p.m., the related customer orders are updated, the missing amount is credited back to the affected customers with an additional 20 percent bonus, and the customers are informed of the delivery problem.

The system maintains a fair-play score for each customer. The score represents the reliability of the customer with respect to previous orders and is used as a precedence criterion when product availability is insufficient. The score is computed from the number of completed orders, reminders received, forfeited pickups, and modified orders. Customers with higher fair-play scores are given precedence over customers with lower scores when limited quantities must be allocated among competing orders.

hlg_1c190ea7f86685cf_001.rationale: llg_001 enables customers to check wallet balance and payment status, which supports awareness of fund availability. llg_002 enables real-time payment notifications, enhancing transparency. llg_003 introduces a grace period mechanism for insufficient funds, adding a customer-centric recovery path. llg_004 and llg_005 define two distinct recharge channels (in-store and online), preserving the modality of payment method and location. llg_006 introduces partial payment capability, which is materially different from full payments and must be explicitly included to avoid misrepresentation of scope.
hlg_1c190ea7f86685cf_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to monitor wallet balances, receive payment notifications, manage insufficient funds with grace periods, recharge wallets via in-store terminals or online transfers, and process partial payments for orders.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Check wallet balance and payment status
Handle insufficient balance with grace period

hlg_45d7b64c9eb54357_001.rationale: llg_001 enables the customer to select a pickup time slot based on store availability; llg_002 ensures the customer receives a reminder notification before the pickup time to confirm attendance; llg_003 ensures the customer is notified if they miss their pickup time and is informed of the forfeit policy consequences — which introduces an unrelated or broader capability (enforcement of policy consequences) that must be explicitly included to expose the mismatch.
hlg_45d7b64c9eb54357_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to schedule, be reminded of, and be notified about missed pickup events for product pickup at stores, including enforcement of forfeit policies upon missed pickups.

hlg_54413bcf2604b197_001.rationale: llg_001 adds transaction recording and payment enforcement; llg_002 adds enforcement of pickup forfeit policies including wallet deductions or marking as forfeited; llg_003 adds automatic fair-play score updates triggered by missed pickups; llg_004 adds fair-play score-based prioritization during shortages; llg_005 adds penalty or bonus management for forfeited orders based on delivery status and behavior. All five capabilities are distinct and must be preserved as they represent different lifecycle phases and outcomes.
hlg_54413bcf2604b197_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Record transactions and enforce payment, enforce pickup forfeit policies, update fair-play scores based on pickup forfeiture, apply fair-play scoring for order prioritization during shortages, and manage forfeited order penalties or bonuses via API.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Update fair-play score based on pickup forfeiture
Apply fair-play scoring for order prioritization during shortages
Manage forfeited order penalties or bonuses

hlg_5c82e14395e9d14b_001.rationale: llg_001 enables automatic prioritization of customer orders during shortages based on fair-play score; llg_002 enables customers to view their fair-play score for transparency; llg_003 enables the system to calculate and update the fair-play score via API using order history, reminders, or penalties. Together, these form a closed-loop system of score computation, display, and prioritization — with no inferred functionality or hidden parent goal.
hlg_5c82e14395e9d14b_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a dynamic customer prioritization system during shortages that calculates, updates, and displays a fair-play score to determine order priority and enable customer self-service visibility.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Prioritize customer based on fair-play score

hlg_5f093c1983a0bd77_001.rationale: llg_001 contributes the capability to allow customers to access and view product origin details, including quality certifications and availability status, which collectively define the complete scope of this high-level goal.
hlg_5f093c1983a0bd77_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to view product origin details, quality certifications, and availability status on product pages.

hlg_8cc6881ea295c041_001.rationale: llg_001 enables the purchasing group representative to submit orders using unique credentials or group ID, establishing the authorization mechanism. llg_002 ensures that before submission, the system verifies the representative’s identity via two-factor authentication or group approval workflow, adding a mandatory verification step. Together, they define a secure, identity-verified order submission process for authorized representatives.
hlg_8cc6881ea295c041_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable authorized purchasing group representatives to submit orders while ensuring their identity is verified before submission.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Authorize group representative to submit orders

hlg_91b57471207e9b44_001.rationale: llg_001 enables customers to submit orders with minimum quantity constraints; llg_002 allows modification of existing orders by altering quantities or items; llg_003 triggers confirmation and system validation; llg_004 introduces a distinct capability to notify customers of availability-driven changes and provide API-based acceptance/rejection, which is materially different from the other goals and must be explicitly included.
hlg_91b57471207e9b44_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to submit, modify, confirm, and receive notifications for order changes due to insufficient availability, while ensuring all orders meet minimum quantity requirements.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Submit an order with minimum quantity
Notify customer of order changes due to insufficient availability

hlg_c12fcb1e0bd72453_001.rationale: llg_001 adds notification to farmers with automatic 20% bonus credit on delays; llg_002 adds notification to customers with estimated resolution time; llg_003 adds automatic 20% bonus credit for missing amounts; llg_004 adds order cancellation and 20% bonus credit for late deliveries — all via API. These capabilities are distinct and must be preserved as they represent different actors (farmer vs. customer), different actions (notify, cancel, credit), and different outcomes (bonus, resolution time).
hlg_c12fcb1e0bd72453_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Automatically notify farmers and customers of delivery delays, cancel late orders, credit back missing amounts with a 20% bonus, and provide estimated resolution times via API.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Automatically credit back missing amount with bonus

decisions.rationale: Transparent and traceable product sourcing is documented.
Efficient order management and allocation is documented.
Seamless payment and wallet management is documented.
Product pickup scheduling and collection is documented.
Accurate inventory and availability tracking for farmers is documented.
Fair and transparent allocation during shortages is documented.
Efficient store operations and order fulfillment are documented.
Timely delivery and customer notification for farmers is documented.
Reliable and fair transactional fulfillment is documented.
Group-based purchasing and representative authorization is documented.

The goal 'Ensure transparent and traceable product sourcing' is documented in the project description, aligning with the system's purpose of supporting a conscious purchasing process based on detailed information about products.

The goal 'Support efficient order management and allocation' is documented in the project description, as evidenced by the system's handling of customer orders, minimum quantity constraints, and prioritization based on fair-play scores during shortages.

The goal 'Enable seamless payment and wallet management' is documented in the project description, as reflected in the system's features allowing customers to manage virtual wallets, receive payment notifications, handle insufficient funds with grace periods, and recharge wallets.

The goal 'Optimize product pickup scheduling and collection' is documented in the project description, evident in the system's provision of time slots for product collection, reminders for missed pickups, and enforcement of forfeit policies.

The goal 'Maintain accurate inventory and availability tracking' is documented in the project description, as farmers are required to submit product availability estimates which the system uses for dynamic allocation and order fulfillment.

The goal 'Support fair and transparent allocation during shortages' is documented in the project description, as the system uses a fair-play score system to prioritize customers during product shortages.

The goal 'Enable efficient store operations and order fulfillment' is documented in the project description, as reflected in the system's features allowing store employees to manage orders, coordinate pickups, handle payments, and confirm delivery status.

The goal 'Provide timely delivery and customer notification' is documented in the project description, as evidenced by the system's alerting of stakeholders to delivery delays, automatic crediting of missing amounts with a bonus, and maintenance of transparency about delivery status.

The goal 'Ensure reliable and fair transactional fulfillment' is documented in the project description, as reflected in the system's enforcement of payment and pickup obligations, application of fair-play scoring for order prioritization during shortages, and management of forfeited orders with penalties or bonuses.

The goal 'Support group-based purchasing and representative authorization' is documented in the project description, as only registered representatives of purchasing groups are authorized to submit orders.

hlg_1c190ea7f86685cf_001.rationale: llg_001 enables customers to check wallet balance and payment status, which supports awareness of fund availability. llg_002 enables real-time payment notifications, enhancing transparency. llg_003 introduces a grace period for insufficient balance, allowing customers to avoid immediate order cancellation. llg_004 enables wallet recharging via in-store terminals, supporting physical access to funding. llg_005 enables wallet recharging via online transfer, supporting digital funding methods. llg_006 introduces partial payment support for orders, enabling flexible payment structures. Together, these capabilities form a comprehensive wallet and payment management system with multiple funding and notification pathways, including a grace period and installment support.
hlg_1c190ea7f86685cf_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to monitor wallet balances, receive payment notifications, manage insufficient funds with grace periods, recharge wallets via in-store terminals or online transfers, and support partial payments for orders.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Check wallet balance and payment status
Handle insufficient balance with grace period

hlg_45d7b64c9eb54357_001.rationale: llg_001 enables customers to select a pickup time slot based on store availability; llg_002 ensures customers receive a reminder notification before pickup to confirm attendance; llg_003 ensures customers are notified if they miss pickup and are informed of forfeit policy consequences — together, these cover the full lifecycle of a pickup appointment including scheduling, notification, and consequence management.
hlg_45d7b64c9eb54357_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to schedule, be notified about, and handle consequences of product pickup appointments at physical stores.

hlg_54413bcf2604b197_001.rationale: llg_001 adds transaction recording and payment enforcement; llg_002 adds enforcement of pickup forfeit policies including wallet deductions; llg_003 adds automatic fair-play score updates triggered by missed pickups; llg_004 adds fair-play score-based prioritization during shortages; llg_005 adds penalty or bonus management for forfeited orders based on delivery status and behavior. All five capabilities are distinct and must be preserved as they represent different lifecycle phases and outcomes.
hlg_54413bcf2604b197_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Record transactions and enforce payment, enforce pickup forfeit policies, update fair-play scores based on pickup forfeiture, apply fair-play scoring for order prioritization during shortages, and manage forfeited order penalties or bonuses via API.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Update fair-play score based on pickup forfeiture
Apply fair-play scoring for order prioritization during shortages
Manage forfeited order penalties or bonuses

hlg_5c82e14395e9d14b_001.rationale: llg_001 adds the capability to automatically prioritize customer orders during shortages using a fair-play score. llg_002 adds the capability for customers to view their fair-play score to understand their priority level. llg_003 adds the capability to calculate and update the fair-play score based on completed orders, reminders, or penalties via API. Together, these form a complete system: score calculation and update (llg_003), score visibility (llg_002), and automated prioritization during shortages (llg_001).
hlg_5c82e14395e9d14b_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a dynamic customer prioritization system during shortages that calculates, updates, and displays a fair-play score based on order behavior, enabling automated prioritization of customer orders and transparent visibility of priority status.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Prioritize customer based on fair-play score

hlg_8cc6881ea295c041_001.rationale: llg_001 enables the purchasing group representative to submit orders using unique credentials or group ID, establishing the authorization mechanism. llg_002 ensures that before submission, the system verifies the representative’s identity via two-factor authentication or group approval workflow, adding a mandatory verification step. Together, they define a secure, identity-verified order submission process for authorized representatives.
hlg_8cc6881ea295c041_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable authorized group representatives to submit purchase orders while ensuring their identity is verified before submission.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Authorize group representative to submit orders

hlg_91b57471207e9b44_001.rationale: llg_001 enables customers to submit orders with minimum quantity constraints; llg_002 allows modification of existing orders by altering quantities or items; llg_003 triggers confirmation and system validation upon finalization; llg_004 introduces a distinct capability to notify customers of availability-driven changes and provide API-based acceptance/rejection options — this capability is materially different and must be explicitly included to expose the scope mismatch.
hlg_91b57471207e9b44_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to submit, modify, confirm, and receive notifications for order changes due to insufficient availability, while enforcing minimum quantity requirements.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Submit an order with minimum quantity
Notify customer of order changes due to insufficient availability

hlg_c12fcb1e0bd72453_001.rationale: llg_001 adds notification to farmers with automatic 20% bonus credit on delays; llg_002 adds notification to customers with estimated resolution time; llg_003 adds automatic 20% bonus credit for missing amounts; llg_004 adds order cancellation and 20% bonus credit for late deliveries — all via API. These capabilities are materially distinct in actor (farmer vs. customer), action (notify vs. cancel vs. credit), and outcome (bonus vs. resolution time vs. cancellation), and none can be generalized or omitted without losing scope.
hlg_c12fcb1e0bd72453_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Notify stakeholders of delivery delays, automatically credit back missing amounts with 20% bonus, cancel late orders, and provide estimated resolution times via API.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Automatically credit back missing amount with bonus
Cancel orders and credit wallets with 20% bonus if deliveries are late

hlg_c1bb6cd286703481_001.rationale: llg_001 enables viewing product origin details including certifications and availability; llg_002 enables browsing farmer-provided product offers with pricing and availability windows; llg_003 enables selecting products and specifying quantities while enforcing minimum order constraints; llg_004 enables submitting orders and triggering system validation of constraints; llg_005 enables receiving automated email summaries post-submission; llg_006 enables viewing optional crop characteristics such as size, ripeness, and certifications. All these capabilities are distinct and must be preserved without generalization or omission.
hlg_c1bb6cd286703481_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to browse farmer-provided product offers, select and specify product quantities while respecting minimum order constraints, submit orders for validation, and receive automated order summaries via email, while also allowing them to view product origin details and optional crop characteristics including certifications and ripeness.

hlg_d714bbf6da86e761_001.rationale: llg_001 enables store employees to view and manage pending orders for fulfillment; llg_002 adds the capability to coordinate pickup logistics including time and location; llg_003 introduces payment processing and wallet balance updates via system API; llg_004 adds the capability to confirm delivery status and update system records. Together, these cover the full lifecycle of order fulfillment from initiation to delivery confirmation, with explicit handling of pickup logistics and payment integration.
hlg_d714bbf6da86e761_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable store employees to manage end-to-end order fulfillment, including coordination of product pickup, processing customer payments, and confirming delivery status via system updates.

hlg_d7aace6841b88a6b_001.rationale: llg_001 enables initial submission of product availability estimates for dynamic allocation; llg_002 adds real-time update capability via API to reflect stock or delivery changes; llg_003 introduces a mandatory Monday-morning confirmation of final quantities available for order, which is a distinct lifecycle phase and deadline not covered by the other goals.
hlg_d7aace6841b88a6b_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable farmers to submit, update, and confirm product availability estimates for dynamic allocation and order fulfillment, with real-time updates and a Monday-morning confirmation deadline.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Confirm final product quantities available for order
